Robotics Engineering · TechTics

Can Crusher

A compact automated can-processing prototype combining sensing, motor control, user interaction and a custom sorting mechanism.

Arduino Encoders Weight Sensing Barcode Scanning Motor Control CAD 3D Printing

Challenge

Automating can handling in a compact prototype

The project explored a smaller automated alternative to large and expensive can-processing machines. The prototype needed to identify incoming cans, verify them using sensor data, move them through the system and provide clear feedback to the user.

My work focused primarily on the mechatronic and digital parts of the system: sensing, motor control, control logic, the user interface and the mechanism used to separate and route cans.

System logic

From inserted can to automated handling

Multiple sensors and actuators were combined into one control flow.

01 Can inserted

The user places a can into the machine.

02 Identify

The barcode scanner identifies the incoming can.

03 Measure

The weight sensor provides an additional physical measurement.

04 Control

Software coordinates the motors using sensor and encoder feedback.

05 Sort

The separation mechanism routes the can through the system.

My contribution

Sensing, control and sorting

  • Integrated barcode scanners for can identification
  • Integrated weight sensors for measurement and verification
  • Used encoder feedback to track mechanism movement
  • Worked on motor control and system sequencing
  • Developed control logic and prototype software
  • Worked on the display and user-interface behaviour
  • Designed and developed the can separation / sorting mechanism
  • Used CAD and 3D printing to iterate physical prototypes
  • Integrated and tested hardware and software as one system
Project scope: I did not design the main crushing mechanism or the enclosure. My contribution focused on sensing, control, the user interface and the sorting parts of the prototype.

Engineering approach

Iterating between digital and physical design

The project required the mechanical prototype, sensors, actuators and software to work together reliably. CAD and 3D printing were used to iterate the sorting mechanism, while sensor feedback and motor behaviour were tested directly on the physical prototype.

This gave me practical experience working across mechanical design, embedded hardware and software rather than treating them as separate systems.
